newsitem.title: BELGIUM: All but Greece, Italy meeting EMU deficit test - EU.
newsitem.headline: All but Greece, Italy meeting EMU deficit test - EU.

text.p: The European Commission painted a rosy view of the pospects for the single currency on Wednesday saying only Italy and Greece were currently missing deficits to growth tests.

Italy was seen running a deficit to Gross Domestic Product ratio of 3.2 percent this year, missing the 3.0 percent target. But the Commission also indicated the deficit next year was set to swell to 3.9 percent of GDP.
The Commission said Germany and France, the two key elements of any economic and monetary union, both looked set to squeeze in with deficits to GDP of 3.0 percent this year.
Spain and Portugal were also running deficits of 3.0 percent.

Release of the Commission figures -- which EU sources and financial analysts say are drafted under tremendous political pressure -- was delayed for close to an hour because of a longer-than-expected debate among members of the Commission.

The Commission said in a statement that although Italy was running a 3.2 percent figure, this could fall to the 3.0 percent target this year if budgetary measures underway -- and possibly new measures -- were effective.
